title: Authorities Investigate the Origin and Destination of Fuel Seized in Guanajuato
author: Anahí Del Ángel
content:
_This article by[Anahí Del Ángel](https://contralinea.com.mx/author/anahida/)
originally appeared in the [September 18, 2026 edition of
Contralínea](https://contralinea.com.mx/interno/semana/investigan-origen-y-
destino-de-combustible-asegurado-en-guanajuato/), a Mexican investigative
journalism magazine._

The operation that made it possible to seize **59 million liters of presumably
illegal fuel** at a property in **Guanajuato** left no one detained;
nevertheless, federal authorities affirmed that there will be captures as a
result of the investigations already underway.

President **Claudia Sheinbaum** indicated that the fuel seizure represents
only one part of the investigation, since the objective is to **identify who
was behind the operation** , as well as to determine **the origin and
destination of the product**.

During the morning presidential press conference, the Secretary of Security
and Citizen Protection, **Omar García Harfuch** , explained that the operation
began on **July 3, 2026** , with the stop of a fuel tanker, from which the
authorities obtained information that led to the property where the fuel was
located.

Faced with the question of why there were no detainees at the search site, he
explained that the property was empty due to the scale of the **mobilization
of federal and state authorities**. "At that moment, there was no one there."

The secretary maintained that the arrests will be carried out later, as the
investigation advances, and asserted that in the other cases of large fuel
seizures, captures have also been made: "of course there are going to be
detainees, but they come afterward."

When asked about the possibility that those who operated the site had received
a **" tip-off"** and abandoned the facilities before the operation, he avoided
offering a conclusion, noting: "we will know with the first arrests."

The seizure also raised questions about the infrastructure found at the
property, because the images released by the **Attorney General 's Office of
the Republic (FGR)** show storage installations that, according to what was
described during the conference, bear similarities to the infrastructure used
by **Petróleos Mexicanos**.

The official explained that it was a storage installation and that later the
Attorney General's Office itself, in coordination with Pemex Physical Security
and Pemex Logistics, will make known what type of infrastructure it was and
what its function was.

He was also asked how it was possible for an installation of those dimensions
to be built and operated without municipal or state authorities noticing. In
response, Harfuch replied that what mattered was that the seizure was
accomplished through a coordinated operation between federal and state
authorities.

Regarding whether the property was operated by the **Santa Rosa de Lima
Cartel** , the secretary declined to speculate, and noted that it will be up
to the Attorney General's Office of the Republic to determine who was behind
the operation, because "right now, giving incorrect information or speculating
would be irresponsible on my part," he maintained.
